unit.title: Guru Arjan Dev Ji and Guru Hargobind Ji

lesson.title: Review Day: Guru Arjan Dev Ji and Guru Hargobind Ji
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: This week you met the fifth and sixth Gurus. Let's review it all!

Quick review: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Adi Granth (Day 1). He also completed Harmandir Sahib and installed the Adi Granth inside it (Day 2). Guru Hargobind Ji introduced Miri-Piri, balancing spiritual and worldly responsibility (Day 3). You built a six-Guru timeline connecting everyone so far (Day 4). Answer: what did Guru Arjan Dev Ji compile, and what does Miri-Piri mean?
Wonderful work these past two weeks! You've built a real, connected timeline of six Gurus and their genuine contributions.

objectives: Review and connect this week's two Gurus: Guru Arjan Dev Ji and Guru Hargobind Ji
State Guru Arjan Dev Ji's compiling achievement and Guru Hargobind Ji's Miri-Piri concept
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child answer both review questions.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing two full weeks of Grade 5 Sikhi — six real Gurus and their contributions!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one of the two Gurus, whichever the child engaged with most this week
Ready for more: ask the child which Guru's contribution from either week they'd most like to learn more about
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's two Gurus needs the most reinforcement
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and review activity — check that the child can state Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Adi Granth and that Miri-Piri means balancing spiritual and worldly responsibility.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's deepened Guru-contributions content before the course continues, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
